expectations.text: Says plainly that the stated constraints eliminate every archetype, instead of forcing one to fit
expectations.evidence: "Direct answer: none of the nine archetypes. Don't run a business model on Glintpad — it isn't a business yet, and forcing one onto it would cost you the thing that's actually working."

expectations.text: States that this means either one of the constraints is wrong or the product is not a business yet
expectations.evidence: "'A constraint that eliminates every archetype means one of the constraints is wrong or the product is not a business yet. Say so rather than forcing a fit.'"

expectations.text: Eliminates hosted SaaS and hosted open source because nothing runs on the vendor's infrastructure and there is no operational burden to sell
expectations.evidence: "Hosted open source | Same deployment constraint, and it fails on its own prerequisite anyway: a stateless single-binary CLI has no operational burden worth paying someone else to carry."

expectations.text: Eliminates dual licensing because the permissive MIT licence provides no forcing function
expectations.evidence: "Dual licensing | MIT is already published — permissive licences make this model impossible by the framework's own rule"

expectations.text: Eliminates source-available because the licence change is refused and no reseller threat exists
expectations.evidence: "Explicitly off the table (public promise never to relicense), and its own prerequisite is also absent: nothing here runs as a service, so there's no hyperscaler-absorption threat"

expectations.text: Eliminates consumption metering because nothing is meterable
expectations.evidence: "Nothing meterable, by your own statement, and structurally impossible anyway — a tool that never touches the network has no channel to observe usage through."

expectations.text: Eliminates the ecosystem take-rate because no third-party ecosystem exists
expectations.evidence: "Ecosystem take-rate | No plugin ecosystem, no second side to the market."

expectations.text: Eliminates open core, support and LTS, and OEM licensing because no organization is present to sign anything

expectations.text: Eliminates hosted SaaS and hosted open source because nothing runs on the vendor's infrastructure and there is no operational burden to sell
expectations.evidence: 'Hosted/SaaS tier — needs a server and network calls. You promised offline-only.'

expectations.text: Eliminates dual licensing because the permissive MIT licence provides no forcing function
expectations.evidence: 'Dual licensing — sells companies an exception to copyleft obligations. MIT has no copyleft to buy out of, and no company has ever asked anyway.'

expectations.text: Eliminates source-available because the licence change is refused and no reseller threat exists
expectations.evidence: The relicensing option is eliminated solely on the grounds that 'You promised never to change the license' — no mention of an absent reseller threat as a second reason.

expectations.text: Eliminates consumption metering because nothing is meterable
expectations.evidence: 'Usage-based pricing — needs telemetry to meter. You touch no network, so you can't see usage even if you wanted to charge for it.'

expectations.text: Eliminates the ecosystem take-rate because no third-party ecosystem exists
expectations.evidence: 'Plugin marketplace / extension revenue share — no plugin ecosystem exists.'

expectations.text: Eliminates open core, support and LTS, and OEM licensing because no organization is present to sign anything
expectations.evidence: Support/consulting is eliminated for lacking 'sales capacity and inbound demand', open core for the license promise, and OEM licensing is not addressed at all — none cite the absence of an organization to sign as the reason.

expectations.text: Names which specific constraint would have to change for any model to become available
